headline: Last session: Indian markets ended higher after rallying up to 2% last week as foreign investors turned buyers.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Monday, 2 November.

why: FPIs turned net buyers last week despite pulling out ₹34,843 crore from equities in October.
October GST mop-up grew 23% year-on-year to over ₹2.31 lakh crore.
IT and Pharma stocks supported market gains during recent trading sessions while midcaps faced pressure.
Crude oil prices remained elevated above $116 per barrel alongside a rise in India VIX.
whatHappening: Oil marketing firms IOC, BPCL, and HPCL reported combined Q2 profits of ₹30,106 crore.
Commercial LPG cylinder prices were hiked by ₹10, while ATF prices were raised by ₹1.37 per litre.
Average daily UPI transaction value crossed ₹1 trillion in October.
Ten penny stocks plunged up to 70% over the last three months.
summary: Indian stock markets are closed today for the weekend and will reopen on Monday, 2 November. Over the past week, Sensex and Nifty rallied up to 2% aided by late foreign inflows and strong Q2 earnings from major oil marketing companies. Macroeconomic indicators remained strong with October GST collections surging 23% to over ₹2.31 lakh crore.
